patches.title: Permission/revocation/recovery executable model specification

invariants.requirement: TLA+ model MUST represent permission -> enqueue -> execution -> crash -> resume, stable effect identity, duplicate delivery, concurrent workers, irrevocable commitment, uncertain completion and reconciliation. A queue item is not enduring permission.

Before commitment, fresh revocation prevents effect; in-flight precommit work is canceled or fenced. After irreversible commitment, revocation prevents new effects and invokes separately authorized containment/compensation/reconciliation; it does not pretend the effect never happened.

Workers and actuator/resource boundaries enforce monotone lease/fencing epochs; stale workers cannot commit under current epoch. Idempotency applies at the effect boundary or unsupported exactly-once guarantees are explicitly absent.

Model outcomes are COUNTEREXAMPLE, COMPLETED_WITHIN_DECLARED_BOUNDS, INCOMPLETE. Incomplete reason identifies state/search-space exhaustion, resource exhaustion, timeout, tool failure, unsupported feature or other explicit reason; incomplete is never PASS.

Receipts bind exact model/configuration identities, assumptions, state/worker/queue/time bounds, checked safety/liveness properties, fairness assumptions, explored-state count and checker version. Completion within bounds is not an unbounded proof.

Every counterexample is investigated as possible design defect, model error, assumption error or property error, retaining trace and adjudication evidence; no dismissal solely because implementation differs.
Runtime recovery tests use matching scenarios and compare observed trace abstractions to allowed model transitions; model-only results do not certify runtime correspondence.

extension_fields: takeover_recoverable_region(D,e): estimated level center in [1.1*D+e,10-1.1*D-e], D>=0 seconds, e>=0 metres; empty if lower>upper; actual initial uncertainty interval [h_hat-e,h_hat+e] must lie within [1.1*D,10-1.1*D]

threshold_proof_obligation: sensor error sign, sampling phase, observation age, monitoring period, remaining handoff delay, actuator dynamics, primary/fallback command ordering, uncertainty interval propagation, numerical discretization error

invariants.requirement: The selected example is a dimensioned abstract tank-level simulation, not a deployment-ready physical safety case. Plant, primary controller, independently implemented fallback, switch, sensor and actuator each have exact versioned profiles and authenticated interfaces.

Primary controller may choose any admitted u within [-1,1]. Worst outward speed is 1.1 m/s. Candidate margin 0.05+1.1*(0.10+0.10+0.20)=0.49m combines measurement error and worst observation age, monitoring phase and handoff delay. This arithmetic is a proposed bound, not validated safety evidence. A continuous-time/interval proof MUST cover error sign, arbitrary sampling phase, delay decomposition without missing or double-counting intervals, threshold comparison semantics, actuator dynamics/latency, competing-command order and numerical discretization error before qualifying switching thresholds.

Fallback pushes inward at net speed at least 0.1m/s at either boundary under stated disturbance/actuator assumptions. This supports an invariant envelope only after timely successful handoff with valid state; it is not a guarantee under actuator failure or violated assumptions.

Define takeover_recoverable_region(D,e) for remaining uncontrolled delay D>=0 seconds and level estimation uncertainty e>=0 metres. Estimated center h_hat must satisfy h_hat in [1.1D+e,10-1.1D-e]; equivalently the actual initial uncertainty interval [h_hat-e,h_hat+e] is contained in [1.1D,10-1.1D]. Reachability over delay expands it to [h_hat-e-1.1D,h_hat+e+1.1D], which must remain in [0,10]. An empty interval is nonrecoverable. [0,10] applies only to exact actual state at completed takeover with D=0 and the specified functioning fallback; it is not an unconditional delayed-handoff entry region. Initial stale observations use full remaining delay and estimation uncertainty.

STPA identifies unsafe control actions at switching: missing/late switch, early return, conflicting controller commands, incorrect state transfer, stale sensor interpretation and unsafe shutdown. Each maps to a constraint, owner and test.

Fallback independence includes control code, execution resources, authority/credentials, sensing and actuation failure assumptions, plus common-cause analysis; shared hardware is explicitly modeled, not silently independent.

Authenticated minimal state transfer binds time, controller, epoch and integrity. Actuator rejects stale primary commands after switch epoch. Failed handoff retains explicit loss-of-assurance and qualified minimum-risk response.

Test outside recoverable region and outside envelope. Choose minimum-risk response under a declared loss function/safety case, e.g. maximum inward control if actuator remains trustworthy; it cannot be described as guaranteed safe when reachability says otherwise.
Return to primary requires root-cause closure, revalidation, fresh authorization, valid envelope and anti-chatter dwell/hysteresis conditions demonstrated compatible with immediate safety override.

Simulation receipts record assumptions, parameter bounds, timing measurements, trajectories, solver discretization error and per-property results; no simulated result is invented by source-design acceptance.

patches.title: Trust boundaries, consistency, interaction hazards and reuse records

invariants.requirement: Identify every component whose compromise/failure can bypass gating, including kernel, runtime, firmware, credential issuer, clock, deployment path and actuator boundary; minimize/isolate this trusted set and explicitly retain residual common-cause risks.

At each capability boundary map authenticated identities, least-privilege authorization, enforcement point and reevaluation triggers; network location or prior successful authentication is not sufficient authority.

Classify objects individually: commutative compatible observations may merge preserving provenance; permission grants/revocations, exclusive resource allocation and authoritative epoch changes require declared coordination/freshness/fencing semantics. Do not apply generic CRDT merges to authority.

Disconnected replicas follow explicit lease expiry/revocation-latency assumptions. Where immediate revocation is required and cannot be checked, new consequential action is blocked; prequalified bounded continuity may continue only under separate valid authority and safety case.

Exclusive resources require epoch/lease-based allocation with fencing at resource boundary and no conflicting reallocation during unresolved ownership; partitions cannot independently mint globally exclusive tickets.

Broader STPA example covers two agents sharing one actuator/resource and a knowledge/clock dependency: conflicting commands, stale authorization, missing coordination and feedback delay yield mapped constraints and scenario tests.
Reuse records retain exact versions, license texts/identifiers, notices and provenance. License identification remains separate from patent assessment; no blanket patent-clearance or ownership claim.
